title: should workload-high has more shares than workload-low?
body:
### What happened?

In my k8s cluster(1.22), the `workload-high` prioritylevelconfiguration has 40 shares and the `workload-low` has 100 shares. Is this correct? I think the `workload-high` should has more shares.

```

leader-election   Limited   10                         16       4          50                 161d

nodes.body: /sig api-machinery
Does this affect any other k8s versions? 1.22 used beta3 of priority and fairness IIRC and is out of support sine 28 Feb 2023

Yes, this affect all k8s versions.
we could find the value defined here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/flowcontrol/bootstrap/default.go#L229
/cc @MikeSpreitzer @wojtek-t

Yes - this is expected.
Workload-high is supposed to be used for high-priority requests, and there aren't that many of those. Workload-low is catching many more requests, and thus by design should have more shares.
thanks @wojtek-t
/triage accepted

title: Numerous incorrect pods caused by specifying node names
body:
### What happened?

When I specifying node names in deployment like below.
```yaml
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      nodeName: node1
      hostNetwork: true
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.14.3
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```
 Something terrible has happened！
SO MANY PODS WAS CREATED!!! until I change the replicas to zero , 131 pods were created and remained, and their status was `failed`
```
  phase: Failed
  message: 'Pod was rejected: Predicate NodePorts failed'
  reason: NodePorts
  startTime: '2023-08-24T14:48:37Z'
```
It seems that pod 's pod was used (previous pod) in target node.


I think we can change the logic of the RS controller to solve this problem, such as not filtering failed pods or determining the specific reason for the failure before deciding when to create a new pod.

I would be happy to provide a PR if our discussion came to an outcome : )

### What did you expect to happen?

failed immediately (no not create so many pods ) or give a hint or warning shows the state that can not be continue handing

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. create deployment with nodeName and hostNetwork,set .spec.replicas greater than one.
   ```
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    metadata:
      name: nginx-deployment
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      replicas: 2
      selector:
        matchLabels:
          app: nginx
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: nginx
        spec:
          nodeName: adam-pro
          hostNetwork: true
          containers:
          - name: nginx
            image: nginx:1.14.3
            ports:
            - containerPort: 80

   ```
2. Waiting for a surge in the number of pods.
    ```
    kubectl get pod --watch
    ```

### Anything else we need to know?

I have try it in many versions of k8s (1.24,1.25, 1.28), all  meet same situation.

When I look into the code,I found `ReplicaSetController` will ignore pod whose status is Failed and create new one.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1d52fb2806e0af468b8b0185f9ba3721d1d2fb3b/pkg/controller/controller_utils.go#L949-959

```go
func IsPodActive(p *v1.Pod) bool {
	return v1.PodSucceeded != p.Status.Phase &&
		v1.PodFailed != p.Status.Phase &&
		p.DeletionTimestamp == nil
}
```
And scheduler's plugin `NodePorts` will be used in kubelet(pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/predicate.go)and `kubelet ` will  set pod's status to fail, as a result `ReplicaSetController` will create pods on and on !
```go
	if !nodeports.Fits(pod, nodeInfo) {
		admissionResults = append(admissionResults, AdmissionResult{Name: nodeports.Name, Reason: nodeports.ErrReason})
		if !includeAllFailures {
			return admissionResults
		}
	}
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L583-L614

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.28.0
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.28.0
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
cluster by kubeadm
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS"
# NAME="Ubuntu"
# VERSION_ID="22.04"
# VERSION="22.04.3 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish)"
# VERSION_CODENAME=jammy
# ID=ubuntu
# ID_LIKE=debian
# HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
# SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
# BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
# PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
# UBUNTU_CODENAME=jammy

$ uname -a
# Linux  6.2.0-26-generic #26~22.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Jul 13 16:27:29 UTC 2 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

</details>


### Install tools

<details>

/sig apps

That seems expected to me.  If you're not a scheduler, you shouldn't be setting nodeName, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#nodename. Specifically you are hitting:

> Bypassing the schedulers might lead to failed Pods if the assigned Nodes get oversubscribed

> That seems expected to me. If you're not a scheduler, you shouldn't be setting nodeName, see

`nodeName is intended for use by custom schedulers or advanced use cases where you need to bypass any configured schedulers. `
As the doc you provided ,some advanced use cases  can set this field , failed Pods were expected, but unlimited creation of pods is unexcepted  and intolerable, It will occupy the full storage of `etcd` which resulting in the unavailability of the entire kubernetes cluster

They should be removed if the number exceeds the `terminated-pod-gc-threshold`, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-garbage-collection .

The default value is 12500 so it may take a while.

> They should be removed if the number exceeds the `terminated-pod-gc-threshold`, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle/#pod-garbage-collection .
> 
> The default value is 12500 so it may take a while.

You can try it locally, ReplicaSetController will create thousands of pods in a minute. 
BTW when it reach 12500  the count of pods will float between 12512 and 12540. I don't think waiting a garbage-collection is a good way.

![mmexport1692933269873.png](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/14191653/db39fbbd-2064-426f-b598-9d4cf6e3139b)

Maybe it has something to do with the behavior of kubelet.
/sig node

Setting nodeName bypasses the scheduler and assigns the pod directly to the node.

If the kubelet observes a pod assigned to it which it does not have resources to run, it marks the pod as failed, which is a terminal state.

A replicaset's job is to ensure that `spec.replicas` pods are active for the replicaset, so it replaces the failed pod with a new one. This is essentially the same issue as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/72593, where the node is rejecting pods, the controller is doing its job keeping N pods active, and the interaction between those two things leads to lots of dead pods until garbage collection kicks in.

Closing this as a duplicate of #72593. One possibility would be backoff behavior in the replicaset controller, though that could be difficult to add without degrading recovery time for scenarios where you *want* failed pods to be quickly recreated.

title: kube-apiserver doesn't clean up OpenAPI properly after deleting an APIService/CRD
body:
### What happened?

I noticed some odd behaviors/logs after deleting APIServices and CRDs.

First, only CRDs were removed from the response of `/openapi/v3` and APIServices were not removed. Not only the root path, the APIService's specific paths were also available, e.g. `/openapi/v3/apis/foo.bar.com/v1alpha1`, as if they were not deleted.

Second, there were some confusing logs in kube-apiserver, indicating it failed to do some cleanup, and every failure was duplicated once:
```
E0822 15:24:36.314675       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1alpha1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.314705       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1alpha1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.316316       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1beta1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.317664       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1beta1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
```

After checking the code, I found the above observations were caused by the same code in kube-apiserver which didn't handle the removal of APIService correctly:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa8cb97f65fe1d24e96eda129337d86109615570/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go#L563-L568

Basically apiserver was calling wrong AggregationController when removing APIService, which caused OpenAPI v3 not cleaned up and the duplicate errors. There was another issue in v2 AggregationController which caused the error. 

Besides, just correcting L567 didn't fix the problem totally, there were some other issues in the implementation.

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-apiserver should clean up OpenAPI correctly, shoud not generate confusing errors.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Install some APIServices and CRDs and remove all of them, then check the response of "/openapi/v3" and kube-apiserver logs.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug


#### What this PR does / why we need it:

There were four issues in OpenAPI aggregation cleanup:
1. When removing an APIService, openAPIAggregationController was called twice while openAPIV3AggregationController was never called, leading to OpenAPI v3 for the APIService not cleaned up.
2. When removing a local APIService, v2 specAggregator should not return ErrAPIServiceNotFound when it doesn't find the APIService because local APIServices were never added to its cache, otherwise confusing error logs would be generated. Besides, the method's comment indicates that the desired behavior is that no error is returned if the APIService does not exist.
3. When removing an APIService, v3 specProxier should update openapiv2converter's cache, like when updating an APIService, otherwise the API would not be removed from "/openapi/v3".
4. When v3 AggregationController reconciles an APIService, it should stop requeueing it if it fails with ErrAPIServiceNotFound as the APIService has been removed, like what v2 AggregationController does, otherwise it would keep reconciling the APIService forever.

Hi @wt-1611

I’m not a maintainer, but there are a few things that I’ve noticed that might be helpful to you. 

First, from the error message on your `svc` object: `Insufficient Node information: allocatable CPU or zone not specified on one or more nodes` - nodes not reporting allocatable CPU can be what's causing this error. Allocatable CPU is used by EndpointSlice to calculate balanced allocations:

```
The controller allocates a proportional amount of endpoints to each zone. This proportion is based on the allocatable CPU cores for nodes running in that zone
```

But I think the bigger problem in your case is that all of your worker nodes are in one zone: `topology.kubernetes.io/zone=b` which makes this feature not relevant for your cluster - all the traffic will have to go to this zone B. Note, that control plane nodes are not taken into account according to the documentation: 

```
The EndpointSlice controller ignores nodes with the node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane or node-role.kubernetes.io/master label set. This could be problematic if workloads are also running on those nodes.
```

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/topology-aware-routing/

Hope that helps

### What happened?

K8S v1.28 rpm builds fail on Fedora 38, 39, and rawhide. These are builds using the establish rpm spec file to create the kubernetes rpms in Fedora. The spec file calls kube::golang::setup_env which is where the error occurs. The error occurs in the new ./hack/tools/ncpu tool.

It is important to note that the spec file sets ```export FORCE_HOST_GO=y```. Fedora 40/39 current provide golang 1.21.0; Fedora 38 provides golang 1.20.7. 

With Fedora 39 and rawhide the following is observed in the build output:

+ GO111MODULE=on
+ go install ./ncpu
go: downloading go.uber.org/automaxprocs v1.5.2
ncpu/main.go:23:2: GOPROXY list is not the empty string, but contains no entries
++ kube::log::errexit
++ local err=1
++ set +o
++ grep -qe '-o errexit'

Something similar to the successful build of K8S 1.27.4 at the same stage in the build process:

/sig api-machinery
/assign

Based on the comments in the [mergeMap](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/63351cce1c1099c64c6c55d540b1e65e947632ad/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch/patch.go#L1360-L1365), this seems to be the expected result

@apelisse I'm not sure if this is a bug or not, but it does cause our results to be inconsistent between the twice apply, was that a conscious decision?
I would think it was not. Most things in strategic-merge-patch were not conscious decision. I'll take a quick look.

I want to see what happens if you run `kubectl apply` one more time. In json-merge-patch, which smp is inspired from, a null value (and in your example, your yaml is equivalent to `baz: null`) means that the field should be removed. The problem here is that you first have a `CREATE` request with the yaml, the null is deserialized as an empty string in the labels. And the second time, you have a PATCH using SMP, the null is interpreted as delete. What happens if you SMP with null again? I guess it's going to do nothing. I don't think there's anything to fix here.
/triage accepted

> What happens if you SMP with null again?

Just tried it 3x, you're correct, the result stays the same.

``` console
$ k get po colorful -ojson | jq '.metadata.labels'
{
  "foo": "bar"
}
```

Interestingly, it says "configured" _every_ time.

``` console
$ k apply -f pod.yaml
pod/colorful configured

$ k apply -f pod.yaml
pod/colorful configured

$ k apply -f pod.yaml
pod/colorful configured
```

> Interestingly, it says "configured" every time.

Yeah, unsurprising to me. To kubectl, it looks like something needs to happen (it needs to send `baz: null`) and the "configured" logic is basically that simple (and inaccurate).

I'm sorry but I don't think there's a bug worth fixing here :-(

The problem is caused by this line:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f0dcf0614036d8c3cd1c9f3b3cf8df4bb1d8e44e/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L250

At that point, `o.config.Logging.Verbosity` is 4 (from the command line flag), and then it gets overwritten with `c.Verbosity` == 0.

The normal approach would be:
- set up config with defaults
- modify config through flags
- modify config further by parsing a config file into it.

Can kube-proxy do this? It has the downside that a config file can only overwrite fields if they are in the file. A config field doesn't get reset to defaults just by parsing the file.

/cc @cyclinder @liggitt @aojea
it looks like kube-proxy special-cases the `processHostnameOverrideFlag` to let a flag override config... can/should it do the same thing for verbosity? are there any other flags like this?

> The normal approach would be:
> 
> * set up config with defaults
> * modify config through flags
> * modify config further by parsing a config file into it.

I don't think that's the normal approach... it's more normal to make flags and config file mutually exclusive. That's difficult for things which started as flags and moved into config

nodes.title: kube-proxy: fix combination of --config and logging command line flags
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When parsing a config file, all settings derived from command line flags are discarded because only the config settings are used. That has been the traditional behavior for non-logging flags.

But `--config ... -v=4` used to work until
71ef0dafa72ca8cf2aa26fe1a75d3379a551771a added logging to the configuration. To restore the original behavior, kube-proxy now:
- parses flags
- reads the config file
- applies logging settings from the flags to the config loaded from file
- uses that merged config

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119864

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Needs more tests...

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
kube-proxy in Kubernetes >= 1.28 up until v1.28.0-beta.0 ignored the `-v` command line flag when combined with `--config`.
```

title: CronJob gets stuck when jobs quota is reached
body:
### What happened?

We (in Booking.com) run CronJobs in Kubernetes clusters with ResourceQuota's defined. When quota for # of jobs is reached we observed that CronJobs:
1. stop scheduling new jobs (because quota is reached),
2. don't clean the old jobs (despite # of jobs > history allows and the fact that it would unblock the CronJob new Jobs). 

The only way to progress is to remove enough Jobs to make room for a new Job in namespace quota. When we do that manually, the CronJob kicks in.

The workaround we found around the internet is to specify `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` for the job template. But it's not ideal as it's not a history-based limit, but a time-based limit, and often you want to have the last N jobs to be around for debugging.

### What did you expect to happen?

When jobs quota is reached and # of cronjob jobs exceeds specified the history limit, these jobs are deleted giving room for new jobs to run.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: job-quota
  namespace: default
spec:
  hard:
    count/jobs.batch: "1"
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-world-cronjob
spec:
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 0
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: hello-world
              image: bash
              command: ["bash", "-c", "sleep 80"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

1. Wait for a first Job to be created (which will fill up the jobs quota) at X minute.
2. A job for X + 1 will fail to be created (because quota won't allow, and X job is still running).
3. All future attempts to create a new job by the controller will fail (check `kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail`, you'll see re-occuring `Error creating job: jobs.batch "hello-world-cronjob-28187648" is forbidden: exceeded quota: job-quota, requested: count/jobs.batch=1, used: count/jobs.batch=1, limited: count/jobs.batch=1`).
4. The first job will never be cleaned (although it will be eligible, since history is 0).

### Anything else we need to know?

Looks like the problem was introduced in the `cronjob_controllerv2.go` implementation: if `jm.syncCronJob` returned an error, we return from the function and never invoke `jm.cleanupFinishedJobs`.:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L199-L213

In the old `cronjob_controller.go` implementation this was not the case:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f77da5bd4809927e15d1658fb4aa8f13ad890a5/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controller.go#L137-L138

title: [It] [sig-network] "Services should create endpoints for unready pods" should not depend on kube-proxy for validation
body:
### What happened?

**[Kubernetes e2e suite: [It] [sig-network] Services should create endpoints for unready pods](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/test/e2e/network/service.go#L1752-L1835)**

This test validates the existence of endpoints of unready pods of a service (with  PublishNotReadyAddresses: true) by probing service with curl requests, in other words depend on kube-proxy to check if the endpoints exists for the service with unready pods. 


### What did you expect to happen?

If I'm not wrong, the purpose of setting `PublishNotReadyAddresses: true` is to make sure the endpoint/endpointslices exists even if the pods are not ready to make sure coredns is able to create A/AAAA records. 

The test should simply check if the endpoints/endpointslices exists for the given service rather than expecting a response from the curl request, i.e. should not depend on kube-proxy.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/test/e2e/network/service.go#L4195-L4196

There are some discussions https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119394#discussion_r1282269250 going on to ignore **Ready**  condition and only use **Serving** and **Terminating** for programming data path. This test becomes a blocker for that task. 


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The test currently passes as kube-proxy currently uses `EndpointConditions.Ready` for programming endpoints. 
Switching from `EndpointConditions.Ready` -> `EndpointConditions.Serving && !EndpointConditions.Terminating` fails the test. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/staging/src/k8s.io/endpointslice/utils.go#L36-L42

title: sched: CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins not always injected into cycleState
body:
### What happened?

In k8s 1.27, scheduler introduced a new "short circuit" semantics in PreFilter to bypass a Pod quickly. A change introduced here is it relies on that plugin to be stored in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins`, which makes sense as what it was explained [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114125/files#r1062646736).

However, the `SkipFilterPlugins` info, although is populated upon each plugin's PreFilter invocation, is not injected into `CycleState` when some PreFilter returns unschedulable:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L655-L661

So think about this workflow:

- pluginA returns Skip in its PreFilter
- pluginB return Unschedulable in its PreFilter
- note: pluginA is not included in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` due to aforementioned bug
- a Pod is claimed as unschedulable (failed by pluginB)
- during PostFilter, it's **supposed** to bypass pluginA's PreEnqueueExtension's AddPod/RemovePod, but it doesn't
- calling a "skipped" Plugin's AddPod/RemovePod during preemption, sometimes will abort the whole preemption as the logic tries to read info from cycleState, and some plugin's "skip" version doesn't fill cycleState properly, e.g., InterPodAffinity (skip immediately w/o write preFilterStateKey).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L257-L262

### What did you expect to happen?

Short circuiting using Skip is fine, but `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` should injected properly at all cases.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Described in the workflow above.

It's firstly captured in an out-of-tree PostFilter plugin: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins/pull/608#issuecomment-1665855370, but can also happen in in-tree plugins.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: kube-proxy still routing to dead coredns endpoint
body:
### What happened?

I know this issue is solved here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/19029 but am still facing it in 1.21 version

Issue:
Envoy is using udp to send DNS requests to coredns. When one of the coredns pods restarts, and this endpoint is replaced by a new one, the envoy is still able to send the DNS requests to the old endpoint, using the same udp socket.

title: CEL Estimated cost incorrect for lowerAscii
body:
### What happened?

Creating a CRD with a case-insensitive uniqueness check and appropriate maxLength/maxItems limits should be allowed:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: uniquetests.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                headers:
                  type: array
                  maxItems: 1
                  x-kubernetes-validations:
                    - rule: "self.all(item1, self.exists_one(item2, item1.name.lowerAscii() == item2.name.lowerAscii()))"
                  items:
                    type: object
                    properties:
                      name:
                        maxLength: 1
                        type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: uniquetests
    singular: uniquetest
    kind: UniqueTest
```

But I got:

```
kubectl apply -f unique.yaml
The CustomResourceDefinition "uniquetests.stable.example.com" is invalid: 
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[headers].x-kubernetes-validations[0].rule: Forbidden: estimated rule cost exceeds budget by factor of more than 100x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared)
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[headers].x-kubernetes-validations[0].rule: Forbidden: contributed to estimated rule cost total exceeding cost limit for entire OpenAPIv3 schema
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema: Forbidden: x-kubernetes-validations estimated rule cost total for entire OpenAPIv3 schema exceeds budget by factor of more than 100x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared)
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the estimated cost to be very low with maxItems=1 and maxLength=1.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This also exceeds the estimated cost limit, suggesting the problem is unrelated to the array:

```yaml
 x-kubernetes-validations:                                                                                        
  - rule: "self[0].name.lowerAscii() == self[0].name.lowerAscii()"
```

But this is valid (estimated cost is under the limit):

```yaml
x-kubernetes-validations:                                                                                        
  - rule: "self.all(item1, self.exists_one(item2, item1.name == item2.name))"
```

Which suggests that the estimated cost system is not handling `lowerAscii` correctly.  The estimated cost of `lowerAscii` should be a function of the input string length (which in this case has a max length of 1), and, for purposes of subsequent cost calculations, the resulting value of `lowerAscii` should be known by the estimated cost system to be the same length as the input string.



### Anything else we need to know?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/library/cost.go#L119 is where the estimated cost of lowerAscii is handled. Just glancing at the code I don't see an obvious problem.

### Kubernetes version

nodes.title: Fixes CEL estimated cost to propagate result sizes correctly
nodes.body:
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes CEL estimated cost to propagate the result size of functions that returns strings/bytes/lists/maps. Without this fix, the estimated size is assumed to be max integer and the estimated cost limit is exceeded, preventing some valid CEL expressions from being used in CRDs for validation. 

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #119749

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

See https://github.com/google/cel-go/pull/787 for the fix to cel-go picked up by this PR. The rest of this PR is tests to ensure the fix applies as expected.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a bug where CEL expressions in CRD validation rules would incorrectly compute a high estimated cost for functions that return strings, lists or maps.
The incorrect cost was evident when the result of a function was used in subsequent operations.
```

title: PodDisruptionBudget with an empty selector `{}` being honored incorrectly
body:
### What happened?

`PodDisruptionBudget` with an empty selector `{}` selects all the pods as expected.
But, during the `drain` /`eviction`, the pdb is not being honored correctly i.e. all the pods are getting evicted.

This issue is only observed with the empty selector and works as expected if a valid label selector is provided that selects all the pods in a namespace.

### What did you expect to happen?

When an empty selector `{}` is provided in the `PodDisruptionBudget`'s spec, the created `PodDisruptionBudget` needs to be honored by not evicting all the pods during the `drain/eviction` api call

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a simple busybox deployment with 3 replicas on a local cluster (or any cluster)
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: busybox
  name: busybox
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busybox
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busybox
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: busybox
        name: busybox
        command: ["sleep", "1000"]
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Always
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

```
- Create a pdb object with an `empty` selector `{}`
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 100%  
  selector: {}
```
- Check the status of the created pdb object that has the `expectedPods` observed to be 3 (which is expected)
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2023-08-02T10:33:29Z"
  generation: 1
  name: pdb
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "495"
  uid: 448b956e-4d2f-4d25-b2c4-202d68d3061d
spec:
  minAvailable: 100%
  selector: {}
status:
  conditions:
  - lastTransitionTime: "2023-08-02T10:33:33Z"
    message: ""
    observedGeneration: 1
    reason: InsufficientPods
    status: "False"
    type: DisruptionAllowed
  currentHealthy: 3
  desiredHealthy: 3
  disruptionsAllowed: 0
  expectedPods: 3
  observedGeneration: 1
```
- Call the `drain` api to see the pdb not being honored and all the pods being evicted
```
$kubectl drain 127.0.0.1 --delete-emptydir-data --dry-run=server

node/127.0.0.1 cordoned (server dry run)
evicting pod kube-system/coredns-6994cbdc59-rqs5s (server dry run)

nodes.title: Fix to honor PDB with an empty selector `{}`
nodes.body:
PDB with an empty selector `{}` is selecting all the pods in a namespace. But, during the `drain`, all the pods are getting evicted which is not expected. This change should fix the issue and honor the pdb before evicting the pods.

Are you planning to work on a fix, Patrick, or should we find a volunteer?

Yes, sorry I'm on vacation and unfortunately I'm not sure when I'm back to work because the [typhoon](https://jp.usembassy.gov/weather-alert-typhoon-khanun/) is blocking all flights from the vacation place. 😢
If no one else has time/a good idea for a quick bug fix, given we're close to the release, can we change the feature gate of the scheduling hint to alpha/disabled by default? I had an idea: if we add `UID` to `PodInfo`, then the code which currently needs to go through the pod pointer no longer needs that pointer. I'll give that a try.

nodes.title: scheduler: fix data race after binding failure
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When binding has failed, `Done` gets called by
`handleBindingCycleError`. Calling it again is at best redundant and worse, suffers from a data race:
- the `assumedPodInfo` is placed in the backoff queue
- an event causes the `Pod` pointer to get updated in it
- reading `assumedPodInfo.Pod.UID` races with that write

This race was found with`go test -race`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #119712

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
kube-scheduler: Fine-grained tracking of events (introduced in 1.28) suffered from a data race when binding fails.
```

title: Service `status.loadBalancer.ingress` can be set when `type` != `LoadBalancer`
body:
xref 119454

I think this may be one of the few cases where we can actually change the behavior in a "breaking" way.

User creates service with `.type=ClusterIP`, `.status.loadBalancer` is empty
Controller or user updates the status subresource, sets `.spec.loadBalancer.ingress[].ip` (not wiped or validated, should be)
User updates `service spec` in any way, `.staus.loadBalancer` is wiped

It's clear that the `.status.loadBalancer` is not meant to be set when `.type` is not "LoadBalancer".

The question is:

1) Fail validation?
2) Silently discard the value?
3) Warn and then discard the value?
4) Just warn and leave it.

Because we allowed it in the past, but it is so volatile, I lean towards 3.

@aojea and @khenidak - the people most familair with this type.

Edit: PrepareForUpdate() runs before warnings.  So:

(1) is easy
(2) is easy
(4) is slightly less easy than (2)
(3) is slightly less easy than (4)

nodes.title: Gate: disallow .status.loadBalancer on non-LB svc
nodes.body:
Fixes #119700

The fact that the .status.loadBalancer field can be set while .spec.type is not "LoadBalancer" is a flub.  Any spec update will already clear .status.ingress, so it's hard to really rely on this.  After this change, updates which try to set this combination will fail validation.

Existing cases of this will not be broken.  Any spec/metadata update will clear it (no error) and this is the only stanza of status.

New gate "AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB" is off by default, but can be enabled if this change actually breaks someone, which seems exceeedingly unlikely.


/kind bug

```release-note
Setting the `status.loadBalancer` of a Service whose `spec.type` is not `"LoadBalancer"` was previously allowed, but any update to the `metadata` or `spec` would wipe that field. Setting this field is no longer permitted unless `spec.type` is  `"LoadBalancer"`.  In the very unlikely event that this has unexpected impact, you can enable the `AllowServiceLBStatusOnNonLB` feature gate, which will restore the previous behavior.  If you do need to set this, please file an issue with the Kubernetes project to help contributors understand why you need it.
```

title: Namespace stuck in Terminating when deleted if ApiService doesn't implement Aggregated Discovery
body:
### What happened?

We implement a manual `APIService` API Extension in [Agones](https://github.com/googleforgames/agones).

Definition:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/install/helm/agones/templates/service/allocation.yaml

Code for handling web requests:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/pkg/util/apiserver/apiserver.go

The code is extremely lightweight as we only have no need for storage, and only accept CREATE requests at this time.

This issue was first reported by one of our users in May, but we only were able to reproduce it ourselves once we were on 1.27.x: https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/issues/3172

Testing on Kubernetes 1.27.x we noticed that when attempting to delete Namespaces, they would get stuck in termination with the following description:

```
❯ kubectl describe ns 1690585578
Name:         1690585578
Labels:       kubernetes.io/metadata.name=1690585578
              owner=e2e-test
Annotations:  <none>
Status:       Terminating
Conditions:
  Type                                         Status  LastTransitionTime               Reason                  Message
  ----                                         ------  ------------------               ------                  -------
  NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure            True    Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:44 -0700  DiscoveryFailed         Discovery failed for some groups, 1 failing: unable to retrieve the complete list of server APIs: allocation.agones.dev/v1: stale GroupVersion discovery: allocation.agones.dev/v1
  NamespaceDeletionGroupVersionParsingFailure  False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:46 -0700  ParsedGroupVersions     All legacy kube types successfully parsed
  NamespaceDeletionContentFailure              False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentDeleted          All content successfully deleted, may be waiting on finalization
  NamespaceContentRemaining                    False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentRemoved          All content successfully removed
  NamespaceFinalizersRemaining                 False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentHasNoFinalizers  All content-preserving finalizers finished
```

So far, I've not found a way to delete the Namespace.

Looking through the log for the webserver, i can see requests for `/apis` and the new Aggregated Discovery feature (`Accept:  "application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList"`), but we return a 404 to that response, since it's not implemented.

Looking through the code I can find (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.3/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go) it seems that any response other than `http.StatusOK` would result in this issue -- which is breaking backward compatibility within `APIService` to assume that this API surface is implemented in some way.


### What did you expect to happen?

Namespaces would terminate as per normal.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install Agones on a cluster (https://agones.dev/site/docs/installation/install-agones/)
2. `kubectl create ns foo`
3. `kubectl delete ns foo`
4. Watch as the ns gets stuck in Terminating.

Will edit this comment as we go, but just writing down some useful notes:

- agones should support the `/apis` endpoint: https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/pkg/util/apiserver/apiserver.go#L130 so it's weird that a 404 is required
- Aggregated Discovery is fully backwards compatible with previous versions. - The issue brought up https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/issues/3172 is on v1.26.5 in which aggregated discovery is disabled (only enabled for 1.27+)

> * Aggregated Discovery is fully backwards compatible with previous versions. A fallback https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.3/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go#L231-L233 is implemented so not supporting aggregated discovery on an APIService will fall back to the old behavior (without the `Accept:  "application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList"` accept header)

That assumes the aggregated server is paying attention to the Accept header, and will respond with a NotAcceptable status code if it doesn't support aggregated discovery... that may or may not be true... ways we could make that stronger / more compatible:

2. send a single request to `/apis` that indicates it accepts BOTH `application/json` and `application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList`, and use the content-type in the returned data to decide whether to go down the aggregated or normal discovery path


 ideally, it would make a single request that indicated it accepted

body:
### What happened? When following the guide *Add ImagePullSecrets to a service account* from the documentation ([here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account/#add-imagepullsecrets-to-a-service-account)), after creating a new secret and configuring the service account with it, public images (ex `nginx`) are still pulled from the DockerHub, without using the custom registry (confirmed by K8S logs and also registry logs) ```console [tbg@host:~] kubectl describe pod nginx | grep Image Image: nginx Image ID: docker.io/library/nginx@sha256:e67bce60872000987d2a86ea0c4338b7e941accfd2ffd1d62ceaf9a100396c97 ``` ### What did you expect to happen? I would expect ALL images (unless a registry is specified) to be pulled from the mirror/cache registry, without having to explicitly specify that registry in the `image: ` field... Here's the result if I start a pod with `--image=registry.fqdn.com/library/nginx` instead of `--image=nginx`, **as stated in the docs** ```console [tbg@Debian:~] kubectl describe pod nginx | grep Image Image: registry.fqdn.com/library/nginx Image ID: registry.fqdn.com/library/nginx@sha256:e67bce60872000987d2a86ea0c4338b7e941accfd2ffd1d62ceaf9a100396c97 ``` ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? ```bash REG_SECRET_KEY=your-key kubectl create secret docker-registry ${REG_SECRET_KEY} --docker-server='registry.fqdn.com' --docker-username='USERNAME' --docker-password='PASSWORD' --docker-email='k8s@registry.fqdn.com' --namespace='default' # Check that secret is created => OK ✅ kubectl get secrets ${REG_SECRET_KEY} kubectl patch serviceaccount default -p "{\"imagePullSecrets\": [{\"name\": \"${REG_SECRET_KEY}\"}]}" # Check that imagePullSecret is configured => OK ✅ kubectl edit serviceaccount/default # Explicit registry url before image name => OK ✅ kubectl run nginx --image=registry.fqdn.com/library/nginx --restart=Never kubectl get pod nginx -o=jsonpath='{.spec.imagePullSecrets[0].name}{"\n"}' kubectl describe pod nginx | grep Image kubectl delete pod nginx # No registry url before image name => KO 🛑 (image comes from docker.io) kubectl run nginx --image=nginx --restart=Never kubectl get pod nginx -o=jsonpath='{.spec.imagePullSecrets[0].name}{"\n"}' kubectl describe pod nginx | grep Image kubectl delete pod nginx ``` ### Anything else we need to know? That doesn't look like a configuration issue, because K8S is able to correctly authenticate to my registry mirror when needed ### Kubernetes version

title: reflector relist when api server upgrade
body:
### What happened? My project use istio as a registry, when k8s api server upgrade or restart, the client-go reflector will do relist and watch, and this can result in a large number of duplicate update events(10w+ events) and pilot handl lager duplicate update events(workloadentry), eventually, the update of Routing table is delayed more then some minutes. ### What did you expect to happen? My expectation is that during api server upgrades or when there are occasional timeout disconnects, the client-go reflector should not perform a relist operation, but instead continue to retry the watch to avoid handling a large number of duplicate update events and cause routing table delayed. **And one of my doubts is why the watch operation is only retried when the connention refused, why not when the connection is closed or connection reset by peer or request timeout?** I think it is safe to retry with last resourceVersion when connection close or timeout, but I'm not sure what details I haven't considered. Refer to this [code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v0.20.1/pkg/client/cache/reflector.go#L171) ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? just restart api server, then you can trigger relist operation ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version

title: api: Finalizer name format is not enforced for custom resources
body:
### What happened?

A client is allowed to add custom finalizers to Custom Resources with a finalizer name that's not fully qualified (e.g. `example` or `example.com`).

However they're prevented from doing the same on builtin resource types, returning the following error:

    Invalid value: "finalizers.compute.linkedin.com": name is neither a standard finalizer name nor is it fully qualified

### What did you expect to happen?

Per [Custom Resource Definition docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#finalizers:~:text=Identifiers%20of%20custom%20finalizers%20consist%20of%20a%20domain%20name%2C%20a%20forward%20slash%20and%20the%20name%20of%20the%20finalizer), custom finalizer names are expected to be in format "consist of a domain name, a forward slash and the name of the finalizer" (e.g. `foo.bar/name`).

Therefore, I expected the enforcement to be the same for CRs and builtin types.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. have a custom resource on the cluster
2. `kubectl edit` it to add `finalizers: [example.com]`
3. observe the edit does not fail
4. do the same on a builtin resource (e.g. Namespace or Pod), observe it fails

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

Reproducible at least starting from 1.21 and still on latest versions.

> @gjkim42 @tzneal  QQ: Why are only the resources of the **restartable** init containers expected to be counted, while normal init containers are not included? Your response is highly appreciated.

The reason we had excluded the normal init containers was that they temporarily occupy resources and release the resources after the initialization phase. However, the restartable init container occupies the resources for the entire lifecyle of the pod.

See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/sidecar-containers/ for the detail.
"Restartable init container" is the internal concept to implement the native sidecar container.

body:

I was replacing kube proxy w/ antrea proxy, our kube proxy replacement.  I found something interesting.... All these rules,

Were still floating around in my cluster.  The problem with this is that i think in the datapath for a linux VM, openvswitch is "After" the IPtables stuff.  So... that means if your replacing kube proxy running in iptables mode w/ another technology, the old service IPs will still be forwarded to potentially old pods that dont exist anymore. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Kube proxy would gracefully  clean up after itself when exiting.  After all, anyone deleting kube proxy is probably doing so with the intent of having at least one pod in their cluster change its IP after a while.  



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a cluster w/ kubeadm and standard kube proxy. 
Delete the kube proxy.
Check `iptables-save` in a node, and youll see all the rules.

### Anything else we need to know?

Maybe as a medium solution we could just have kube proxy delete things that are specific to pod IPs.

This is probably all overkill but i figured i should write this issue up in case others hit the same thing when trying to swap out kube proxy for another service proxy in a running cluster. title: Restore Kubernetes API service endpoint during HA rolling restarts
body:
### What happened?

I think that https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115804 via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116685 have introduced a regression for HA Kubernetes API server configurations behind a proxy and/or load balancer.  Such configurations may only have a single Kubernetes API server endpoint that should not be removed during a rolling restart of the Kubernetes API server.

**Example:**
```
$  kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers
kubernetes   172.20.0.1:2040   48m
```

### What did you expect to happen?

`kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers` will remain unchanged throughout the HA rolling restart of the Kubernetes API server.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run the following script during an HA rolling restart of the Kubernetes API server:

```
while true; do date && kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers; sleep 1; done
```

You will see `kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers` return `kubernetes   <none>` several times during this rollout.

### Anything else we need to know?

Nothing

### Kubernetes version

<details>

Could you take a look at this? Thank you.

>  Such configurations may only have a single Kubernetes API server endpoint that should not be removed during a rolling restart of the Kubernetes API server.

The endpoint should only be present when the apiserver is ready to serve traffic, the HA setup, assuming a loadbalancer,  should poll the apiserver /healthz endpoint before sending traffic to the apiserver.

The problem is that if the endpoint exist but there is no apiserver it will be blackholing traffic (that was the bug)

Is not the problem here that the rolling update is not well synchronized, leaving a time window where there is no apiserver ready ?

tagging @deads2k as he is very experienced in this area too
@aojea from an HA availability perspective, I did not see any problems that would justify removing the endpoint.

>  I did not see any problems that would justify removing the endpoint.

dropping traffic is not a problem?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115804

> If the IP isn't removed from the k8s endpoints object, clients (using in-cluster API mode) will try to continue talking/connecting to that instance even after the apiserver is dead. There are at least two issues with this:

> Causes confusing i/o timeout and connection refused errors for clients, instead of a cleaner no route to host error

@aojea dropping traffic is a problem but our Kubernetes API server configuration is HA and traffic is not being dropped.  The problem that we are seeing now is the in cluster applications using the kubernetes service will hit errors during the rollout because the endpoint is being removed 3 times during the rollout (once per API server).  There's really no reason to remove it.
@aojea I repeated my test on 1.26 where the endpoint is not removed, and traffic is not dropped for the kubernetes service during an HA rolling restart.
Hi folks, are there any updates on this issue?
the apiserver, when shutting down should remove its endpoint and add it back once it is ready again after restart, that is the expected behavior

@aojea I'm not sure how to interpret your response with respect to this issue.  The behavior changed for the worse for the use case that I described.  Is there something that we should be doing to handle this change for our use case?

> Is there something that we should be doing to handle this change for our use case?

How do you implement ha? Haproxy or some sort of load balancer?

The point is that anything that implements HA in front of the apiservers , haproxy, routing anycast, keepalived + whatever, ... has to take into consideration the /healthz endpoint of the corresponding apiserver/backend, if the backend is not ready/healthy then the HA implementation must not forward traffic to it

@aojea agreed and we do that.  We use haproxy in conjunction with other tools to manage this.  Having Kubernetes remove the endpoint impacts our design and would appreciate at least an option to maintain the original behavior.

> We use haproxy in conjunction with other tools to manage this. Having Kubernetes remove the endpoint impacts our design and would appreciate at least an option to maintain the original behavior

but the endpoint is only removed when the healthz endpoint does not reply, so your haproxy should be removing it out of rotation and not forwarding traffic to it, that is the part I do not understand, sending traffic to that endpoint is invalid because that backend is no longer present

At this point I think there is some miscommunication at some place, do you have a repro or link to a job testing this  or to the code that implement the HA so I can be able to fully understand all the details?

@aojea I spoke with the networking folks on my side and they wanted me to pass along the following information.

Our configuration uses haproxy on cluster worker nodes to listen locally on the Kubernetes API server's service cluster IP endpoint and forward traffic to one of the three Kubernetes API server endpoints behind a cloud zone endpoint. In Kubernetes version 1.27 and earlier, haproxy would see the endpoint go up and down and handle accordingly.  Now in Kubernetes version 1.28, this still happens but we now also temporarily lose the endpoint thus preventing in cluster components from reaching haproxy and thus the Kubernetes API server.

```
$  kubectl get endpoints kubernetes --no-headers
kubernetes   172.20.0.1:2040   48m
```

Here is a basic diagram of the use case

```
                                                                                   /---- API server endpoint 1
in-cluster component ---> default/kubernetes service --->  haproxy 172.20.0.1:2040 ----- API server endpoint 2
                                                                                   \---- API server endpoint 3
```

do they have something like this? (I copy pasted from internet, just highlight they need to set the health checks)

```
backend apiserver
  option httpchk

  http-check connect
  http-check send meth GET uri /health
  http-check expect status 200

  server server1 endpoint1:443 check
  server server2 endpoint2:443 check
  server server3 endpoint3:443 check
```

wait 

>. this still happens but we now also temporarily lose the endpoint thus preventing in cluster components from reaching haproxy

> in-cluster component ---> default/kubernetes service --->  haproxy 172.20.0.1:2040 

this is confusing , how do you inject service -> haproxy in between? it is service -> endpoints

Yes, the `default/kubernetes` clusterIP service only endpoint is 172.20.0.1:2040.  And that IP and port 2040 is where our local haproxy is listening on each worker (we implement that as a static pod on each worker).  Here's the actual output from a cluster:

[classic-iks-cluster-output.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/12285060/classic-iks-cluster-output.txt)

For the sake of this discussion, I don't think the details of what the haproxy (pod) on each worker is actually pointing to, but if it is needed I can get into more details.  The haproxy configuration does use a health check so it only sends traffic to the backend apiserver instances (pods) that are responding, but I think that also is besides the point.  The point I think is that we set the kubernetes clusterIP service to point to a single endpoint IP:Port:

```
bradbehle@Brads-MacBook-Pro ~ % kubectl get services
NAME         TYPE        CLUSTER-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)   AGE
kubernetes   ClusterIP   172.21.0.1   <none>        443/TCP   26m
bradbehle@Brads-MacBook-Pro ~ % kubectl get endpoints kubernetes -o wide
NAME         ENDPOINTS         AGE
kubernetes   172.20.0.1:2040   25m
bradbehle@Brads-MacBook-Pro ~ % 
```

and that endpoint:port takes care of making sure to only send traffic to apiservers that are up and running.  This was all working fine in k8s 1.27 and earlier.  But now in k8s 1.28, it seems that when only one of the three apiserver instances for this cluster is restarted, that endpoint is (temporarily) removed from the service, which prevents the service from routing to the endpoint which is still able to route traffic to the other two apiserver instances.  That is a serious problem for us because it prevents components in the cluster from connecting to our apiserver even when it has 2 valid instances that are running and can be health checked successfully.

who creates this endpoint `endpoint is 172.20.0.1:2040` ?

The apiserver has an endpoint reconciler that is configurable, by default is the `Lease` controller
```
--endpoint-reconciler-type string     Default: "lease"
```

this reconciler updates the Endpoint object with the IPs of each apiserver, this does not seems to be your use case, so you may be creating it yourself?

if that is the case you have to use `--endpoint-reconciler-type none`

@aojea we have `--endpoint-reconciler-type lease` which I think means all three Kubernetes API servers are creating the same endpoint.  That would explain why I see the endpoint get recreated soon after one of the API servers deletes it.  Given this, it sounds like we should be using `--endpoint-reconciler-type none` and creating the endpoint ourselves.  I'll give this a try.

@aojea after changing our cluster deployment configuration to use `--endpoint-reconciler-type none` and to create the endpoint and endpointslice ourselves, we no longer hit the reported issue.  Thank you for your assistance.

> @aojea after changing our cluster deployment configuration to use `--endpoint-reconciler-type none` and to create the endpoint and endpointslice ourselves, we no longer hit the reported issue. Thank you for your assistance.

Thanks for the constructive discussion, glad your issue is solved

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Prevent potential concurrent map access by taking a lock before reading the topology cache's `hintsPopulatedByService` map.

* `staging/src/k8s.io/endpointslice/topologycache/topologycache.go` (`setHintsLocked`, `hasPopulatedHintsLocked`): New helper functions.  These are the same as the existing `SetHints` and `HasPopulatedHints` methods except that these helpers assume that a lock is already held.
(`SetHints`): Use `setHintsLocked`.
(`HasPopulatedHints`): Take a lock and use `hasPopulatedHintsLocked`.
(`AddHints`): Take a lock and use `setHintsLocked` and `hasPopulatedHintsLocked`.

body:
### What happened?

nodes.body: /sig network
/assign @danwinship

/triage accepted
/cc @uablrek 

So I've never looked at the ipvs graceful termination code before, but it seems to do this intentionally? When adding a "new" endpoint that is already in the graceful delete list, proxier.go calls `proxier.gracefuldeleteManager.MoveRSOutofGracefulDeleteList`, which calls `m.ipvs.DeleteRealServer` and removes the endpoint from the list. Then proxier.go creates a new endpoint.

Maybe this is just a dumb mistake, but there's an explicit comment explaining this behavior ("`// check if newEndpoint is in gracefulDelete list, if true, delete this ep immediately`") so it seems pretty intentional... maybe there's some reason why setting the weight back to 1 instead of 0 doesn't work? Lars? Anyone?

If not, it seems simple enough to fix: `MoveRSOutofGracefulDeleteList` should just be basically the inverse of `GracefulDeleteRS`.

/area kube-proxy
/area ipvs

I think the "shutdown" in graceful shutdown is taken literally. The POD is supposed to terminate. If it comes back to ready, some error is assumed and the endpoint is removed/reinserted just in case.

But to make a POD not-ready for a while, for example on an overload, is a valid use-case. IMO the weight should be restored.

How does proxy-mode=iptables handle this? I suppose it just update the iptables load-balancing, and the conntracker make sure existing connections are unaffected. If so, that is another reason for ipvs to behave in a similar way.
@andrewsykim May know more

iptables mode doesn't have to explicitly think about this; it just removes the iptables rule when the endpoint becomes unready, but the conntrack rules will make already-open connections keep working. So if the endpoint comes back it just adds the iptables rule back again, and again, existing connections are left untouched.

If keeping the sysctl parameter below disabled as its default value, ipvs retains existing connections even if the ipvs entries associated with the connections are removed in this particular case.

```
expire_nodest_conn - BOOLEAN
        0 - disabled (default)
        not 0 - enabled

        The default value is 0, the load balancer will silently drop
        packets when its destination server is not available. It may
        be useful, when user-space monitoring program deletes the
        destination server (because of server overload or wrong
        detection) and add back the server later, and the connections
        to the server can continue.

        If this feature is enabled, the load balancer will expire the
        connection immediately when a packet arrives and its
        destination server is not available, then the client program
        will be notified that the connection is closed. This is
        equivalent to the feature some people requires to flush
        connections when its destination is not available.
```

The parameter is however set to 1 explicitly in the ipvs proxier for some reasons. 

```go
	// Set the expire_nodest_conn sysctl we need for
	if err := utilproxy.EnsureSysctl(sysctl, sysctlExpireNoDestConn, 1); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
```
It can be disabled to support this use-case in the same way that iptables proxy-mode behaves. Though, I'm not sure if the change conflicts with any other use-cases.

@sondinht That is another use-case. The set to 1 is correct. When a server drops out the client want's to know. This is about weight. It is set to 0 when a pod is not-ready, and when the pod becomes ready again the endpoint is removed/reinserted instead of simply setting weight=1, which is likely the correct action.

@danwinship @uablrek 
I traced this back to the origin, the original reviewer wanted the destination removed from the queue (_not deleted_) and the weight set to 1 rather than deleting and creating the destination again.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/66012#discussion_r201287351

nodes.title: Volume resource requirements
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/kind api-change
/sig storage

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

PVC and containers shared the same ResourceRequirements struct to define their
API. When resource claims were added, that struct got extended, which
accidentally also changed the PVC API. To avoid such a mistake from happening
again, PVC now uses its own VolumeResourceRequirements struct.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115845

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The struct has to have a `Claims` field because someone might have added it to
some YAML file for use with Kubernetes 1.28 even though it didn't do
anything. Removing the field in Kubernetes 1.29 would cause OpenAPI-based
validation in kubectl to reject such a YAML file.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Go API: the ResourceRequirements struct needs to be replaced with VolumeResourceRequirements for use with volumes.
```

title: kubelet client cert is not getting auto-rotated (K8s 1.21)
body:
### What happened?

Deployed Kubernetes on a single node setup (master+worker). The setup was UP, checked Kubelet + certs managed by Kubeadm has a validity of 1yr. Now, changed the date of the system to 30% of the cert's expiry date. 

Ran Kubeadm certs renew all, certs managed by Kubeadm got renewed from the day to the next year on the same date. 
but Kubelet client cert "/var/lib/kubelet/pki" is not auto-rotated still pointing to old certificate. 

Waited for 1day, still didn't get rotate. 

**As mentioned in the k8s official document**
As the expiration of the signed certificate approaches, the kubelet will automatically issue a new certificate signing request, using the Kubernetes API. This can happen at any point **between 30% and 10%**f the time remaining on the certificate. Again, the controller manager will automatically approve the certificate request and attach a signed certificate to the certificate signing request. The kubelet will retrieve the new signed certificate from the Kubernetes API and write that to disk. Then it will update the connections it has to the Kubernetes API to reconnect using the new certificate.



Also tried below setup to manually generate or rotate client certificate.

Call 'kubeadm init phase kubeconfig kubelet' optionally pass -config or other flags if needed. This will generate kubelet.conf with embedded cert and key.
Restart kubelet and wait for it to generate new certs in /var/lib/kubelet/pki
Call 'kubeadm init phase kubelet-finalize all'. This will 'symlink' the kebelet.conf to kubelet cert rotation.
Restart kubelet again.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102556

new certs didn't get generate. 


### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet certs should get auto-rotate. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Deploy k8s, and change the date to 30% of the expiry date of the certificate. and wait for kubelet to auto-rotate the client certificate.

title: VolumeZone scheduling plugin should handle csi migration
body:
### What happened?

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268, we discovered that our plan for eventually removing the [VolumeZone](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumezone) scheduling plugin when CSI migration is GA is not possible because the plugin also applies to non-migratable volume types.

However, if we leave the plugin as is, then even migratable PVs will be broken if we remove beta topology labels from Nodes in the future. This is because the plugin does not have any handling for migrated volumes.


### What did you expect to happen?

I suggest we add CSI migration handling to the VolumeZone plugin. I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In a cluster with csi migration for a specific intree volume type enabled,
1. create an intree PV with beta topology labels
2. remove the beta topology label from a node
3. try to schedule a pod using that pv

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

For e2e testing, this needs an environment that is configured with csi migration

Hi,I'd like to work on this issue. I previously wrote `PreFilter` for `volume_zone` plugin, so I'm familiar with it's logic. However I'm not familiar with the whole `CSI` thing, and I may ask you some questions during the work :(  
Can I try this one?
***
Here are some questions ahead:
I think what you want to do is to schedule a pv with old labels to a node with only new labels.
And you think we can translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` in volume_zone during `PreFilter`(maybe), and update this pv so that in `Filter` stage, `volumebinding` can `CheckNodeAffinity`, so we don't have compare Topology labels in `volume_zone`.

My question is:
>  For migrated volumes, we translate PV.Labels into PV.NodeAffinity

Can't we just translate this for all pvs? Why do we need to detect if the volume is migrated? What's the difference between a migrated pv and a non-migratable pv in this scenario?

> Can't we just translate this for all pvs? Why do we need to detect if the volume is migrated? What's the difference between a migrated pv and a non-migratable pv in this scenario?

I think this is also another alternative solution that could also work, but from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268#issuecomment-1337414393, it may not scalable to do an automatic migration for all the different APIs and controllers that use the node labels. The main difference with CSI migration, is we have a good idea of all the different components that would be impacted and also have reasonable control over those components.

> I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate PV.Labels into PV.NodeAffinity so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

A few more questions😂

1.  > detect if the volume is migrated

Will the volumes be migrated before we take a pod off the scheduler queue? If so, how can I detect this. Currently I find a function `IsPVMigratable` in `csi-translation-lib`, but nothing like  `IsPVMigrated`.

2.  > For migrated volumes, we translate PV.Labels into PV.NodeAffinity

Is this translation  done in `volume_zone` plugin or before scheduling?

3.  I think currently in `volume_zone`, we consider topology label and beta label as different labels. That is ,if we have a pv with `LabelFailureDomainBetaZone` and a node with `LabelTopologyZone`, even if they have same values, `volume_zone` will `not` let the pod pass filter. If we're going to remove beta labels on node,maybe we should try to consider two labels as the same in `volume_zone`?
***
Here's my understanding:
- For migrated volumes, we translate Topology labels to pv.NodeAffinity and update the pv, then we skip volume_zone(that is,don't compare labels with nodes).
- What about non-migratable volumes, I think we should continue to compare pv.labels with node labels for non-migratable volumes?

For detecting if a PV is migrated, you can use the same method that's used in the VolumeBinding plugin: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding/binder.go#L1129. The only difference is you don't actually need to translate the PV in the VolumeZone plugin since it's already handled by the VolumeBinding plugin.

For non-migratable volumes, I think we can continue with the same VolumeZone logic. For now, we'll rely on users to update their PVs with the GA labels.

Thanks @msau42 ,for your detailed explanation. This is the implementation plan I prepared:
In `volume_zone prefilter`, we check if a pv is migrtable by using `IsPVMigratable`,if so we skip volume_zone since `volume_binding` will translate this pv and handle it later, otherwise we save the label of this pv in state,and compare it with node's label in `filter`.Is that feasible to you?
Yup that sounds good to me!

In the meantime, I think I previously wrote a bug in `volume_zone` plugin😢, I wonder if you have time to confirm it #115052

title: apiserver crashes with dual-stack service CIDRs if primary range does not match `kubernetes.default` Public IP family in k8s >= 1.24
body:
### What happened?

apiserver crashes at startup if using dual-stack service CIDRs but the primary service CIDR family does not match the IP family of the advertised address.

#106721 introduced validation that checks the service CIDR is the same IP family as the advertised public address of apiserver. It assumes single-stack scenarios and does not check `ExtraConfig.SecondaryServiceIPRange`

### What did you expect to happen?

This should not block apiserver to come up. AKS has been testing clusters with the IPv6 service CIDR as primary with an IPv4 public IP with no issues until 1.24. Example of the kubernetes default service with IPv6 cluster IP but IPv4 endpoint.

```
Name:              kubernetes
Namespace:         default
Labels:            component=apiserver
                   provider=kubernetes
Annotations:       <none>
Selector:          <none>
Type:              ClusterIP
IP Family Policy:  SingleStack
IP Families:       IPv6
IP:                fdff:ffff:1234:6754::1
IPs:               fdff:ffff:1234:6754::1
Port:              https  443/TCP
TargetPort:        443/TCP
Endpoints:         52.188.128.76:443
Session Affinity:  None
Events:            <none>
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a dual-stack cluster using k8s 1.24 with an IPv4 public IP and order the service-cluster-ip-range argument to apiserver such that IPv6 is first (e.g. `--service-cluster-ip-range="fdff:ffff:1234:6754::/108,100.64.0.0/16"`. Apiserver will fail to come up with a similar error message

```
I0803 14:48:27.991658       1 flags.go:64] FLAG: --advertise-address="20.21.22.23"
I0803 14:48:27.992806       1 flags.go:64] FLAG: --service-cluster-ip-range="fdff:ffff:1234:6754::/108,100.64.0.0/16"
E0803 14:48:30.149624       1 run.go:74] "command failed" err="error creating bootstrap controller: service IP family \"fdff:ffff:1234:6754::/108\" must match public address family \"20.21.22.23\""
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I think we should update `pkg/controlplane/controller.go` to also check the secondary service IP range during the reconciliation.

>= 1.24

The block you posted is suspicious:

```
Name:              kubernetes
Namespace:         default
Labels:            component=apiserver
                   provider=kubernetes
Annotations:       <none>
Selector:          <none>
Type:              ClusterIP
IP Family Policy:  SingleStack
