```

You have a Service with a v6 "frontend" and a v4 "backend".  We specifically do not support that - we can't convert between families.

It sounds like the bug is that apiserver reconciled itself according to the default rules used for any service (single-stack, primary family == IPv6) without considering the `--advertise-address`.  It seems reasonable that we use the same family as the `--advertise-address` if that family is available.

Is that the correc reading of this bug?

@thockin interesting, I did not realize this wasn't supported. TIL. The clusters we've done this on have only been test clusters where nothing reaches out to the apiserver from within the cluster so it was never noticed. We will make sure to set the IPv4 CIDR before the IPv6 in the args for clusters using an IPv4 advertise address. Do you think a bug needs to be filed for earlier k8s versions to prevent apiserver from reconciling itself like this? The PR from @aojea I linked in this issue should take care of it for 1.24 and greater.

Yeah, the problem is that using that configuration leaves the cluster unusable because of

> Service with a v6 "frontend" and a v4 "backend"

All InCluster communications use the "kubernetes.default" service. The clusters boots but controllers or apps that use the apiserver Service fail, creating a lot of confusion to users, since it is not easy to understand why the applications fail.


This KEP should fix this https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2622

> Do you think a bug needs to be filed for earlier k8s versions to prevent apiserver from reconciling itself like this?

1.23 at max, that is when [ dual stack went GA](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/dual-stack/)

I can't remember why I didn't backport it, but it is probably I forget, feel free to do it

What we are doing now is clearly wrong.  apiserver should not set this up.

I think it's reasonable to consider whether to use the non-primary range when `--advertise-address` is within that, or else actually cause an error saying they do not match.

> What we are doing now is clearly wrong. apiserver should not set this up.

What is wrong? Who should configure the endpoint or current fix?

Let's take a look and how this works

1. The bootstrap of the apiserver creates a Service that is SingleStack with name "kubernetes.default" using the first IP of the Primary service ip range, this was decided during dual stack to keep backwards compatibility, creating the notion of Primary ServiceIPRange

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e6d6409cf873b0eac47216ff6061387d9c38b002/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/options/options.go#L74-L75

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bd9444c1cfd438690dc21c31404dd79ab60dc6cb/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/server.go#L539-L547

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d82f98c9b3dbbdf7daed2a17fb44ecc3ac7d23ad/pkg/master/master.go#L95-L96

2. If you use the endpoints reconciler (this case) it will use the configured `--advertise-address` as the endpoint IP for the "kubernetes.default" service.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bd9444c1cfd438690dc21c31404dd79ab60dc6cb/pkg/controlplane/controller.go#L126

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bd9444c1cfd438690dc21c31404dd79ab60dc6cb/pkg/controlplane/controller.go#L155-L156

If the families doesn't match,  you have a broken cluster. 
We had a lot of bug reports because of this, reports are like: "I have some things that doesn't work within the cluster, pods restart with connection timeout trying to connect to service kubernetes.default ...."

Users and devs are not able to identify this problem easily, troubleshooting it requires knowing how apiserver bootstrap works and the Dual-stack Services/Endpoints relations , nobody is checking that the Service and the Endpoint IP family doesn't match, I mean, why on a connection timeout are you going to think that the problem is that :upside_down_face: 




```
$ kubectl get services
NAME         TYPE        CLUSTER-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)   AGE
kubernetes   ClusterIP   10.96.0.1    <none>        443/TCP   45h
$ kubectl get endpoints
NAME         ENDPOINTS         AGE
kubernetes   172.18.0.2:6443   45h

```

> I think it's reasonable to consider whether to use the non-primary range when `--advertise-address` is within that, or else actually cause an error saying they do not match.

Then you have to change the convention to assign the IP to the "kubernetes.default" Service, and that has a lot of implications, @danwinship covers this topic more in detail in his KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/2438-dual-stack-apiserver

If your concern is "how did we get there, we could have done better" I agree, but changing this right now seems complicated and is better to fail fast (the config is invalid) than leaving a cluster with an unusable "kubernetes.default" Service, with all the things it implies
Yeah, the fix for now is probably "require that `--advertise-address` matches the primary service address family".
Agree

> Yeah, the fix for now is probably "require that `--advertise-address` matches the primary service address family".

is not as easy, we need to match the primary ServiceIPRange family, that comes from the flags, with the `advertise-address` that does not necessarily come from a flag, and usually is derived from the host IP (the IP obtained from the interface with the default route)

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ae62cd6ce2a61a6252c62a1de7a7061a2484a477/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/server_run_options.go#L104-L120

there is also the problem that --advertise-address` can use the unspecified address to favor one or the other family during the "discovery", but does not necessarily mean that the obtained IP will match it

... and, only if the flag `--endpoint-reconciler-type` is set, if is `none`, the endpoints are not generated by the apiserver, are generated externally

```
--endpoint-reconciler-type string     Default: "lease"
--
  | Use an endpoint reconciler (master-count, lease, none) master-count is deprecated, and will be removed in a future version.
```

`--endpoint-reconciler` doesn't matter (in the sense that, if you try to manually set endpoint IPs of the wrong family, it won't actually work).

The "kubernetes" Service will _always_ have a clusterIP from the primary service CIDR, therefore the "kubernetes" Endpoints/EndpointSlice must also have IPs from the primary service CIDR's family or the apiserver service won't work, therefore anything else that redirects traffic to either the "kubernetes" clusterIP or its endpoint IPs must also be using the primary IP family.

> `--endpoint-reconciler` doesn't matter (in the sense that, if you try to manually set endpoint IPs of the wrong family, it won't actually work).

my point is that we only panic if we know that we are going to do something wrong

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bd9444c1cfd438690dc21c31404dd79ab60dc6cb/pkg/controlplane/controller.go#L98

if the endpoint reconciler is not set there is no check

title: Kubelet creates leases without ownerReference set if node doesn't exist
body:
### What happened?

* Some external controller deleted node object while kubelet was alive
* Due to ignoring errors in kubelet's lease logic, it created lease without ownerReference set

### What did you expect to happen?

* Kubelet doesn't create lease without ownerReference set in any case, even pathological one

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Some external controller deletes node object
* Garbage collector properly deletes associated lease object
* Kubelet tries to update object and it fails on Conflict (saying that UID doesn't match): 
  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L179-L198
* We go to `apierrors.IsConflict(err)` branch, call backoffEnsureLease and assign result to base, but backoffEnsureLease may return potentially invalid object if ensureLease returned error (which happens when newLeasePostProcessFunc returns error, e.g. when node doesn't exist).
* We `continue`
* The next loop calls c.newLease on the incorrect base and ignores error in line 181 (so the second attempt to call newLeasePostProcessFunc which also fails with an error) 
* We do UPDATE with incomplete (without effect of newLeasePostProcessFunc) object
* Given that leases allow CreateOnUpdate a new object, without ownerReference is created: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/pkg/registry/coordination/lease/strategy.go#L65-L68

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

/triage accepted

need to understand what is the right behavior here

We are in trouble for this problem too. 

I think It’s exactly as @mborsz said.
Lease has the special update endpoint which can create the new lease objects not only update them.
If it receives a request with a new lease object which has non-nil UID field, **returns a conflict error**.

This situation can be occured in the [retryUpdateLease](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6ed938fc8f3a9d99e5e0347c57055678891739a4/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L177-L198) function when a lease object is deleted.  The lease object is deleted when the node resource is deleted in the result of GC.

When received a conflict error in updating a lease object and the parent node object doesn't exist, [the base variable is set with nil by the ensureLease function](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6ed938fc8f3a9d99e5e0347c57055678891739a4/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L189-L192), and continue next loop. In the next loop, the [newLease](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6ed938fc8f3a9d99e5e0347c57055678891739a4/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L181) function returns the new lease object without ownerReference and UID. As a result, it is created unexpectively by the special update endpoint.

body:
### What happened?

We have kubernetes 1.20.8/9 with rke2. If we spawn like 100 new pods each mounting only a single pvc like this:
```
volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /mnt

E0208 15:56:39.797423    3771 pod_workers.go:190] "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="unmounted volumes=[vol-3689], unattached volumes=[vol-3689]: timed out waiting for the condition" po

title: Kube-apiserver high memory usage on pending pods storm
body:
**What happened**:
The kube-apiserver consumed memory spiked to ~90G the moment we upscaled the cluster with +400 nodes while having thousands of pending pods.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2542264/105851679-1722a880-5fec-11eb-9517-081e77c029a2.png)
This resulted in OOM kill of the kube-apiserver pods causing outage. Example:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2542264/105851827-43d6c000-5fec-11eb-8d36-3ec6b92c8365.png)

**What you expected to happen**:
The kube-apiserver should not consume that much memory resulting in OOM. I understand that under the presented conditions there could be performance penalties on kube-apiserver or kube-scheduler delaying the pods' startup, but it should not lead to OOM kill.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Have a deployment with pods requesting for 4CPU and 4G MEM
2. Scale the deployment to a huge number of replicas: 2000
3. Prevent the CA to autoscale the cluster (i.e. uninstall the cluster-autoscaler/scale it to 0 replicas)
4. Wait for ~30min-1h (there is no pattern here, it could happen even faster)
5. Manually scale the cluster out to 400 nodes
6. Monitor the kube-apiserver MEM usage

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This in conjunction with cilium and contour+envoy could lead to ingress failures.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"16", GitVersion:"v1.16.2", GitCommit:"c97fe5036ef3df2967d086711e6c0c405941e14b", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2019-10-15T23:41:55Z", GoVersion:"go1.12.10", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"18", GitVersion:"v1.18.14", GitCommit:"89182bdd065fbcaffefec691908a739d161efc03", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-12-18T12:02:35Z", GoVersion:"go1.13.15", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
`AWS`
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
```

title: pod.status.containerStatuses displayed image name incorrectly when image has multiple tags on the node
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!-->


**What happened**:
image name in `pod.status.containerStatuses` is different from `pod.spec.containers` via `kubectl get pod -o yaml`
**What you expected to happen**:
image name in should be the same in `pod.status.containerStatuses` and `pod.spec.containers`
**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. give a new tag to a image via `docker tag` (same image with different tag)
2. start a deployment using that image with original tag
3. show pod yaml via `kubectl get pod -o yaml <pod name>`
we will see the image name in `pod.status.containerStatuses` is the new tag rather than the original tag we have set in the spec

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
``` bash

title: detach volumes from nodes when nodeShutdown is applied
body:
As planned for 1.12 in kubernetes/features#551:

After #60009, the next step is to add the logic to the reconciler to detach the volumes when the nodeShutdown taint is applied.

/assign
/sig storage
/kind feature

looping @jingxu97

nodes.body:
How do you know that node is Shutdown?
is it a planned shutdown or a unplanned shutdown?

@shay-berman AFAIK regardless of whether it's planned or not, it's detected by the cloud provider.

In case of bare-metal node it doesn't happen automatically, as there is no universal way to reliably determine if a node is powered off, so the node must be tainted as `nodeShutdown` by some external source.
